sources.entry: py7zr - A pure-Python library for reading and writing 7-Zip archives.

summary.one_liner: py7zr is a pure-Python library and command-line tool for reading, writing, encrypting and decrypting 7-Zip archives.
summary.what_it_does: py7zr provides a SevenZipFile class for reading and writing 7z archives from Python code, including extractall, extract with selected targets, getnames, and writeall, plus a context manager interface. It also ships a CLI with subcommands to list (l), extract (x), test (t), create (c), append (a), show info (i), and print version, with optional password prompts and multi-volume output via -v. Supported compression methods include LZMA2, LZMA, Bzip2, Deflate, Copy, ZStandard, Brotli, PPMd, and an experimental Enhanced Deflate, along with 7zAES encryption and Delta and BCJ filters. The library can register itself with Python's shutil module for make_archive and unpack_archive. The README notes that some optional algorithms rely on third-party packages listed in its dependency table. Documentation is linked to a user guide and API guide, and a 2022 path traversal vulnerability is described with a recommendation to upgrade to 0.20.2 or later.
use_cases: Extract a 7z archive from a Python script
Extract selected files from a 7z archive
Compress a directory into a 7z file with zstandard or other filters
Use 7z support through shutil.make_archive or unpack_archive
Install Qt or other packages distributed as 7z files
notable: Pure-Python implementation of the 7z format, with a SevenZipFile API and a py7zr CLI
Extracts into memory through a factory/Py7zIO callback interface (replaced read/readall in 1.0.0-rc2)
Registers as a format handler for Python's shutil archive functions
Includes a CVE-2022-44900 path traversal fix in version 0.20.2
caveats: Slower than native 7-zip and p7zip; the README recommends subprocess calls to those tools when speed matters
Needs roughly 300-700 MiB of free memory for typical compression and decompression
ZStandard and Brotli archives are not compatible with the original 7-zip tools, and BCJ2 is not supported
Versions 0.20.0, 0.19.0, 0.18.10 and earlier have a path traversal vulnerability
